title.zh: 卷264 列傳五十一 郝维讷 任克溥 刘鸿儒 刘楗 张廷枢
title.en: Volume 264 Biographies 51: Hao Weine, Ren Kepu, Liu Hongru, Liu Jian, Zhang Tingshu
title.raw: 卷264 列傳五十一 郝维讷 任克溥 刘鸿儒 刘楗 张廷枢

sentences.zh: 郝維訥，字敏公，直隸霸州人。

translations.literal: Hao Weine, style name Min'gong, was a native of Bazhou in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Weine, whose courtesy name was Mingong, came from Bazhou in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 父傑，明崇禎進士。

translations.literal: His father Jie was a jinshi in the Chongzhen reign of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jie had passed the metropolitan examination in the Chongzhen era of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 順治初，授行人，遷戶部給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he was appointed Bearer of Dispatches and promoted to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shunzhi reign he was made a Bearer of Dispatches, then promoted to a revenue supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 迭疏請開經筵，祀闕里，廢斥諸臣才堪錄用者量予自新，朝賀大典內監不得入班行禮，俱下部議行。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized to convene the imperial lecture hall, sacrifice at Qufu, grant measured rehabilitation to dismissed officials whose talents warranted reuse, and bar eunuchs from joining the ranks at grand court celebration rites; all were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: In successive memorials he urged opening the imperial lecture series, restoring sacrifices at the Confucius temple in Qufu, allowing dismissed officials of proven ability a measured path back to service, and barring eunuchs from the formal ranks at great court ceremonies—all sent to the relevant ministries for deliberation and enactment.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several postings to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 維訥，順治四年進士，授刑部主事，再遷郎中。

translations.literal: Weine passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Shunzhi, was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice, and was twice promoted to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: Weine took his jinshi in Shunzhi 4, entered the Ministry of Justice as a principal secretary, and was promoted twice to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 七年，出為福建督糧道僉事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was sent out as assistant surveillance commissioner of the Fujian grain-supervision circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he went out to Fujian as assistant commissioner on the grain-supervision circuit.

sentences.zh: 師下漳南，糧運多阻，維訥督米二萬石浮海達泉州以濟軍。

translations.literal: When the army advanced south of Zhangzhou, grain transport was largely obstructed; Weine supervised twenty thousand piculs of grain shipped by sea to Quanzhou to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial forces pushed into southern Zhangzhou, supply lines faltered; Weine oversaw twenty thousand piculs of grain sent by sea to Quanzhou to feed the troops.

sentences.zh: 巨盜張自盛犯延、卲，徙維訥權延建卲道，設方略，用間散其黨，自盛就擒。

translations.literal: The great bandit Zhang Zisheng raided Yanzhou and Shaowu; Weine was transferred to serve concurrently as commissioner of the Yanjian-Shaowu circuit, devised strategy, used agents to break up his faction, and Zisheng was captured.
translations.idiomatic: The outlaw Zhang Zisheng harried Yan and Shao; Weine was moved to act as Yanjian-Shaowu commissioner, laid plans, sowed discord among Zhang's followers with spies, and took him alive.

sentences.zh: 尋署按察使，謝苞苴，絕羨耗。

translations.literal: Soon after he was acting provincial judicial commissioner; he declined gift-giving and cut off surplus extractions.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as acting provincial judicial commissioner, refusing gifts and ending illicit surcharges.

sentences.zh: 舉卓異，復用孫承澤、成克鞏薦，十一年，召授通政司右參議。

translations.literal: Rated outstanding in performance, and again recommended by Sun Chengyao and Cheng Kegong, in the eleventh year he was summoned and appointed right vice commissioner of the Court of Imperial Supplications.
translations.idiomatic: Cited for outstanding service and recommended again by Sun Chengyao and Cheng Kegong, in the eleventh year he was recalled and made right vice commissioner of the Court of Imperial Supplications.

sentences.zh: 累遷大理寺卿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in stages to president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 十三年，擢戶部侍郎，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was elevated to vice minister of revenue and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he became vice minister of revenue, then was shifted to personnel.

sentences.zh: 十六年，丁父憂。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起戶部侍郎，復調吏部。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was reappointed vice minister of revenue and again transferred to personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he returned as vice minister of revenue and was again transferred to personnel.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，典會試，尋擢左都御史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi he presided over the metropolitan examination and was soon promoted to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 3 he chaired the metropolitan examination and was soon made left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 維訥以開國二十餘年，南徼初定，民困未蘇，疏言：「天下大弊在民窮財盡，連年川、湖、閩、廣、雲、貴無不增兵增餉，本省不支，他省協濟。

translations.literal: Weine, noting that more than twenty years since the founding the southern frontiers had only just been pacified and the people's hardship was not yet relieved, memorialized: "The great ill of the realm lies in the people's poverty and the treasury's exhaustion; year after year in Sichuan, Huguang, Fujian, Guangdong, Yunnan, and Guizhou troops and pay have been increased without cease; the home province cannot sustain it and other provinces must assist."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that more than twenty years after the dynasty's founding the southern marches had only just settled and popular distress had not eased, Weine wrote: "The gravest malady under Heaven is destitution among the people and exhaustion of the treasury. Year after year Sichuan, Huguang, Fujian, Guangdong, Yunnan, and Guizhou have all added troops and stipends; when a province cannot bear the cost, others must help pay."

sentences.zh: 臣觀川、湖等省尚多曠土，若選綠旗及降兵精銳者隸之營伍，給以牛種，所在屯田，則供應減而協濟可以永除，閭里無追呼之困。

translations.literal: Your subject observes that Sichuan, Huguang, and other provinces still have much idle land; if elite Green Standard and surrendered troops were selected, enrolled in garrisons, and given oxen and seed for local garrison farming, then supply costs would fall, mutual aid levies could be ended for good, and neighborhoods would be free of the distress of press-gangs.
translations.idiomatic: "I find that Sichuan, Huguang, and the like still hold much uncultivated land. Choose the best from the Green Standard and surrendered units, place them in camps, give them cattle and seed, and farm where they are posted—then local supply falls, cross-province subsidies can cease forever, and villages escape the torment of repeated summons for grain."

sentences.zh: 」又疏言：「巡按既裁，地方巡視責歸督撫。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "Since the touring censors were abolished, responsibility for local inspection has fallen to governors-general and governors."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "With touring censors gone, provincial oversight rests on governors-general and governors."

sentences.zh: 督撫任重事繁，出巡動逾旬月，恐誤公務，況騎從眾多，經過滋擾。

translations.literal: Governors-general and governors bear heavy duties and many affairs; when they tour the field it often exceeds ten days and a month, which may delay public business; moreover their mounted retinues are numerous and their passage breeds disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Their burdens are heavy and their dockets full; an inspection tour commonly runs more than ten days and risks neglect of routine business—not to mention the large escorts that harass every place they pass.

sentences.zh: 至屬官貪廉，閭閻疾苦，諮訪耳目，仍寄司道。

translations.literal: As for the probity of subordinate officials and the hardships of the people in lanes and alleys, the ears and eyes for inquiry still rest with the circuit intendants and prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Whether subordinates are corrupt or upright, and what pain the common people suffer, still depend on circuit and prefectural officials for intelligence.

sentences.zh: 請嗣後事關重大者，仍親身巡察，餘概停止。

translations.literal: Henceforth, he requested, only matters of great weight should be inspected in person; all else should cease.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that hereafter governors go out in person only for matters of the first importance and stop the rest.

sentences.zh: 」又疏言：「山西、山東等省偏旱，發帑賑濟，聖恩至為優渥，特窮鄉僻壤恐難遍及，惟蠲免錢糧，率土均霑實惠。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "Shanxi, Shandong, and other provinces suffered partial drought; funds were issued for relief and the imperial grace was exceedingly generous, yet remote hamlets may be hard to reach; only remission of land tax and grain levies lets the whole realm share the real benefit."
translations.idiomatic: He further wrote: "Shanxi, Shandong, and others have been partly stricken by drought. The court has opened the treasury for relief with extraordinary grace, yet the poorest villages may never see an inspector. Only exempting land tax and grain dues spreads the benefit evenly across the realm."

sentences.zh: 但田有田賦，丁有丁差，前者被災地方，例多免糧不免丁；

translations.literal: Yet land has land tax and households have corvée levies; in disaster areas the rule often remits grain tax but not corvée;
translations.idiomatic: But fields carry land tax and households carry corvée: in stricken districts custom often waives grain tax yet still collects corvée;

sentences.zh: 其有丁無田者，反不得與有田之戶同霑恩澤。

translations.literal: those who owe corvée but hold no land cannot share the imperial favor with landholding households.
translations.idiomatic: householders with corvée obligations but no fields thus fail to share the same grace as landowners.

sentences.zh: 請丁銀均如田糧分數蠲免。

translations.literal: He requested that corvée silver be remitted in the same proportion as land grain.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that corvée payments be reduced in the same fractions as land grain.

sentences.zh: 」又疏言：「貪吏罪至死者，遇赦免死，並免交吏部議處。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "Corrupt officials sentenced to death who meet an amnesty are spared execution and also spared referral to the Ministry of Personnel for disposition."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "When corrupt officials condemned to death receive an amnesty, they escape the noose and also escape personnel review."

sentences.zh: 此曹饕餮狼藉，未可令其復玷名器，貽害地方。

translations.literal: Such men are gluttonous and lawless; they must not be allowed again to stain official regalia and harm the regions.
translations.idiomatic: These men gorge and trample the law; they must not be allowed back into office to harm the provinces again.

sentences.zh: 雖新例赴部另補，貪殘所至，播虐惟均。

translations.literal: Although under the new rule they may go to the ministry for another appointment, wherever greed and cruelty go, suffering spreads equally.
translations.idiomatic: Even under the new rule they may seek another post at the ministry; wherever the greedy and cruel are sent, misery follows in equal measure.

sentences.zh: 請敕部定議，凡贓款審實者，遇赦免罪，仍當奪官。

translations.literal: He requested that the ministry be ordered to fix the rule: whenever embezzlement is proved on review, even if an amnesty remits the crime, office must still be stripped.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the ministry to decree that whenever embezzlement is proved, amnesty may spare the life but must still strip rank.

sentences.zh: 庶官箴可肅，民害可除。

translations.literal: Then official discipline may be tightened and the people's harm removed.
translations.idiomatic: Only then can official discipline be restored and popular injury ended.

sentences.zh: 」皆下部議行。

translations.literal: " All were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All these proposals were sent to the ministries for deliberation and enactment.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷工部尚書，調刑、禮二部。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to minister of works and then to the ministries of justice and rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he became minister of works, then was shifted to justice and rites.

sentences.zh: 八年，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was moved to revenue.

sentences.zh: 疏請停督撫勘災，申禁圈取民地，並得旨允行。

translations.literal: He memorialized to stop governors-general and governors from personally surveying disasters, and to forbid the enclosure of commoners' land; the throne approved both.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to end governors' personal disaster inspections and to ban seizures of civilian land for banner estates; both received imperial assent.

sentences.zh: 十一年，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was transferred to personnel.

sentences.zh: 時兵興開捐納，正途日壅，維訥為斟酌資格，按缺分選，銓法稱平。

translations.literal: At that time war had led to the opening of purchase offices; the regular path of advancement was daily blocked; Weine weighed qualifications, assigned posts by vacancy category, and the selection law was called fair.
translations.idiomatic: With war came sale of offices and the regular route to promotion grew clogged; Weine balanced qualifications and matched candidates to vacancy types, and the selection system was praised as even-handed.

sentences.zh: 十八年，給事中姚締虞請寬免科道風聞言事之禁，下廷臣議，維訥謂：「言官奏事，原不禁其風聞。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year supervising secretary Yao Diyu asked that censors be relieved of restrictions on reporting hearsay; the matter was referred to court officials for discussion; Weine said: "Censorial memorials were never forbidden on grounds of hearsay."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Yao Diyu asked to relax rules on censorial hearsay reports; the court debated it. Weine said: "Memorialists were never barred from raising hearsay in the first place."

sentences.zh: 但風聞奏參審問全虛者，例有處分，否則慮有藉風聞挾私報怨者，請仍照定例行。

translations.literal: But when impeachment on hearsay was investigated and wholly false, there was precedent for punishment; otherwise one feared those who used hearsay to settle private scores; he asked that the established rules still apply.
translations.idiomatic: "But when a hearsay impeachment is tried and proves wholly false, punishment follows by precedent—otherwise men will use rumor to settle private scores. I ask that the standing rules remain."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The throne assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 維訥領吏、戶二部最久，法制多經裁定。

translations.literal: Weine headed the ministries of personnel and revenue longest, and many regulations passed through his final judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Weine led personnel and revenue longer than any other portfolio, and much of the administrative code passed under his hand.

sentences.zh: 凡事持大體，遇會議、會推、朝審，委曲斟酌，期於至當。

translations.literal: In all matters he held to the larger pattern; at joint conferences, joint recommendations, and court review of capital cases he weighed every angle with care, aiming at what was right.
translations.idiomatic: He always kept the larger design in view; at conferences, joint recommendations, and capital reviews he weighed each side until the outcome was just.

sentences.zh: 敷奏條暢，所見與眾偶有同異，開陳端緒，不留隱情，上深重之，往往從其言。

translations.literal: His memorials were orderly and fluent; when his view occasionally differed from others he laid out the thread of the matter and concealed nothing; the emperor valued him deeply and often followed his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He presented memorials with clarity and flow; when he differed from colleagues he traced the issue to its root and held nothing back. The emperor trusted him deeply and often took his advice.

sentences.zh: 十九年，遭母憂。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he mourned his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，詣京師，未補官，卒，諡恭定。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he went to the capital, was not yet reassigned to office, and died; his posthumous title was Gongding.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he came to the capital, had not yet received a new appointment, and died; he was given the posthumous name Gongding.

sentences.zh: 任克溥，字海眉，山東聊城人。

translations.literal: Ren Kepu, style name Haimei, was a native of Liaocheng in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Kepu, courtesy name Haimei, was from Liaocheng in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 順治四年進士，授南陽府推官。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fourth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed investigating magistrate of Nanyang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Shunzhi 4 and was made investigating magistrate of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 卓異行取，十三年，授吏科給事中。

translations.literal: Selected for outstanding service, in the thirteenth year he was appointed supervising secretary in the personnel section.
translations.idiomatic: Marked for outstanding service and brought to the capital, in the thirteenth year he became a personnel supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「上勵精圖治，知親民之官莫過守令，特擇各府繁劇難治者，許三品以上各舉一人，破格任用。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Your Majesty is striving to govern well and knows that no officials are closer to the people than prefects and magistrates; you have specially chosen the most difficult and crowded prefectures and allowed each official of the third rank and above to recommend one man for extraordinary appointment."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Your Majesty labors to bring order and knows that no officials touch the people more directly than prefects and magistrates. You have singled out the busiest, hardest prefectures and allowed each minister-grade officer to nominate one man for exceptional appointment."

sentences.zh: 使保舉得當，一人賢則一郡安，人人賢則各省安，太平何難立致。

translations.literal: If recommendations are sound, one worthy man brings one commandery peace; if every man is worthy, every province is secure—how hard can lasting peace be to achieve?
translations.idiomatic: "If the choices are right, one good man steadies a whole commandery; if every choice is right, every province is calm—lasting peace would follow of itself."

sentences.zh: 乃為時未久，以貪庸劾罷者已有數人，前此保舉不能秉公慎選可知。

translations.literal: Yet in so short a time several men already impeached for greed and mediocrity show that earlier recommendations could not have been made with impartial care.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet in so little time several nominees have already been dismissed for greed or incompetence—proof that earlier recommendations were not made with impartial care."

sentences.zh: 乞敕部察處。

translations.literal: He begged that the ministry be ordered to investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the ministry investigate and discipline those responsible.

sentences.zh: 十四年，轉刑科，疏言：「抗糧弊有三：宦戶、儒戶、衙蠹。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he transferred to the penal section and memorialized: "The evils of resisting grain tax fall into three: official households, scholar households, and yamen parasites."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he moved to the penal section and wrote: "Resistance to grain payment has three sources: official households, scholar households, and yamen parasites."

sentences.zh: 宜分三項，各另造冊，申報總督、巡撫、巡按，宦欠者題參，衿欠者褫革，役欠者逮治。

translations.literal: They should be divided into three registers, each separately compiled and reported to the governor-general, governor, and touring censor; official arrears should be impeached, gentry arrears should bring stripping of status, and clerk arrears should bring arrest and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: "Split them into three lists, each reported to governor-general, governor, and censor; impeach official debtors, strip gentry debtors of rank, and arrest clerk debtors."

sentences.zh: 」复疏論順天鄉試給事中陸貽吉與同考官李振鄴、張我樸交通行賄鬻舉人，下吏部、都察院嚴鞫，貽吉、振鄴、我樸與居間博士蔡元禧，進士項紹芳，行賄舉人田耜、鄔作霖皆坐斬。

translations.literal: " He again memorialized on Shuntian provincial examiner Lu Yiji and fellow examiners Li Zhenye and Zhang Wopu trading bribes to sell juren degrees; the case was sent to the ministries of personnel and justice and the Censorate for strict interrogation; Yiji, Zhenye, Wopu, the go-between Erudite Cai Yuanxi, jinshi Xiang Shaofang, and bribe-paying candidates Tian Si and Wu Zuolin were all sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: He also exposed Lu Yiji, Li Zhenye, and Zhang Wopu in the Shuntian provincial examination for taking bribes to sell juren ranks. The case went to personnel, the Censorate, and justice for harsh inquiry; Lu, Li, Zhang, the broker Cai Yuanxi, the graduate Xiang Shaofang, and the candidates Tian Si and Wu Zuolin were all executed.

sentences.zh: 命禮部覆試不及程者，褫奪流徙又二十五人，考官庶子曹本榮、中允宋之繩並坐降調。

translations.literal: Those who failed the Ministry of Rites re-examination for not meeting standards were stripped of degrees and banished, twenty-five more; examiners Expositor Cao Benrong and Reader Song Zhisheng were also demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates who failed the Ministry of Rites re-test were disqualified and exiled—twenty-five more. Examiners Cao Benrong and Song Zhisheng were demoted as well.

sentences.zh: 十五年，充會試同考官，出闈，疏言：「伏讀上諭，令各衙門條奏興利除弊。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he served as associate examiner of the metropolitan examination; leaving the examination compound he memorialized: "Having read Your Majesty's edict ordering every yamen to submit items for promoting benefit and removing harm."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was associate metropolitan examiner; on leaving the compound he wrote: "I have read Your Majesty's order that every office list measures to advance the public good and remove abuses."

sentences.zh: 時近兩月，僅見宗人府一疏，各衙門遲疑觀望。

translations.literal: Nearly two months had passed and only one memorial from the Court of the Imperial Clan had appeared; every office hesitated and watched.
translations.idiomatic: "Nearly two months have passed and only the Imperial Clan Court has memorialized; every other office waits and watches."

sentences.zh: 竊謂其病有二：一則因循既久，發論方新，恐無以贖往日曠官之咎；

translations.literal: Your subject believes there are two ailments: one is that long inertia makes a fresh policy frightening, lest one cannot atone for past dereliction;
translations.idiomatic: "I see two sicknesses: long habit makes a new policy frightening, lest one cannot answer for years of neglect;"

sentences.zh: 一則瞻望多端，指陳無隱，恐無以留後來遷就之門。

translations.literal: the other is that many considerations make frank speech risky, lest one close the door to later compromise.
translations.idiomatic: "and many considerations make plain speech dangerous, lest one shut the door to later evasion."

sentences.zh: 臣子報國，止有朴忠，遇事直陳；

translations.literal: A subject serves the state only with plain loyalty and speaks straight when matters arise;
translations.idiomatic: "Serving the throne demands plain loyalty and direct speech when issues arise;"

sentences.zh: 稍一轉念，便持兩端，勢必摭拾瑣屑，剿說雷同，不能慷慨論列，又安望設誠致行？

translations.literal: with the slightest second thought one holds two positions, must pick trifles, and parrot others—how can one argue boldly, and how can one hope for sincere action?
translations.idiomatic: "the moment one hesitates, one straddles two sides, gathers trivia, and repeats what others say—how then can one speak boldly, and how can policy be carried out in earnest?"

sentences.zh: 乞嚴飭不得浮泛塞責，並鑑別當否，示以勸懲。

translations.literal: He begged strict orders against empty compliance and judgment of right and wrong as encouragement and warning.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for strict orders against empty compliance and for reward and punishment according to whether proposals were sound.

sentences.zh: 」又疏言：「近以各衙門胥役作姦犯科，詔令諸臣計議指摘。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "Recently, because clerks in various offices committed crimes, an edict ordered officials to plan exposure and correction."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Because clerks in many offices have lately committed crimes, Your Majesty has ordered officials to plan how to expose and correct them."

sentences.zh: 臣以為懲於弊後，不若杜於弊先，如吏部文選司推升原有定序，應先懸榜部門，序列姓名、資俸、薦紀、參罰，使共見共聞；

translations.literal: Your subject believes that punishing after the abuse is inferior to stopping it beforehand; as in the Ministry of Personnel's Bureau of Appointments, promotions follow a fixed order and a placard should first be posted at the gate listing names, salary grades, recommendations, and penalties for all to see;
translations.idiomatic: "Punishment after the fact is weaker than prevention. In the Appointments Bureau promotions follow a fixed sequence: post the list at the gate with names, salary, recommendations, and penalties for all to see;"

sentences.zh: 考功司議處條例，亦畫一頒發，使不得輕重增減。

translations.literal: the Bureau of Evaluation's rules for disposition should also be issued uniformly so that severity cannot be arbitrarily increased or reduced.
translations.idiomatic: "issue the Evaluation Bureau's penalty rules in one uniform text so severity cannot be twisted up or down."

sentences.zh: 至各官開缺，以科鈔為憑，向以發鈔後先轉移舞弊。

translations.literal: As for vacancies, section memorials are the authority; formerly after memorials were issued the order could be shifted to enable fraud.
translations.idiomatic: "For vacancies the section memorial is the warrant; after issue the order could be rearranged to allow fraud."

sentences.zh: 如當逮問，先下刑部，與事止奪官、迳下吏部者遲速有異。

translations.literal: When arrest and trial are required, sending first to the Ministry of Justice differs in speed from cases where only dismissal is involved and the case goes straight to personnel.
translations.idiomatic: "When arrest is required, sending first to justice differs in speed from cases of dismissal only sent straight to personnel."

sentences.zh: 應令即日鈔發，使不容操縱。

translations.literal: Memorials should be issued the same day so that manipulation is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: "Memorials should be issued the same day so no one can manipulate the queue."

sentences.zh: 」上以所奏切中時弊，下部詳議行。

translations.literal: " The emperor, finding the memorials hit the abuses of the time, ordered detailed deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found these points struck at current abuses and ordered the ministries to deliberate and enact them.

sentences.zh: 轉禮科都給事中，疏言：「士為四民首，宜端習尚。

translations.literal: He transferred to chief supervising secretary of the rites section and memorialized: "Scholars are the head of the four classes of people and should uphold proper conduct."
translations.idiomatic: He became chief supervising secretary of the rites section and wrote: "Scholars stand at the head of the four orders of society and should keep their conduct upright."

sentences.zh: 請敕學臣，凡有請託私書，許揭送部科，差滿定為上考。

translations.literal: He asked that educational commissioners, whenever private letters soliciting favor arrive, be allowed to forward them to the ministry sections, and that at term's end this be rated top performance.
translations.idiomatic: "Let educational commissioners forward any private letters of solicitation to the ministries, and count that as top merit at the end of term."

sentences.zh: 並令舉優當訪學行著聞之士，懲劣則以抗糧為最重。

translations.literal: In recommending the excellent they should seek men of renowned learning and conduct; in punishing the inferior, resistance to grain tax should weigh heaviest.
translations.idiomatic: "When recommending the excellent, seek men of real learning and reputation; when punishing the unworthy, treat grain resistance as the gravest offense."

sentences.zh: 」又疏言：「錢糧逋欠，非盡在民。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "Arrears in tax and grain are not all among the common people."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Tax arrears are not all owed by commoners."

sentences.zh: 臣前奏三款，部議分冊申報，得旨允行；

translations.literal: Your subject's earlier three-category memorial was deliberated by the ministry for separate registers and reporting, and received imperial assent;
translations.idiomatic: "My earlier three-category proposal was approved for separate registers and reporting;"

sentences.zh: 而造冊奏報者，惟山西一省耳。

translations.literal: yet only Shanxi province compiled and reported registers.
translations.idiomatic: "yet only Shanxi has actually compiled and reported them."

sentences.zh: 諸省玩洩從事，不肯實心清理，徒以開荒增課，一時博優敘之榮，仍聽其逋欠而不之問，請飭部察覈；

translations.literal: Other provinces treated the matter slackly and would not earnestly clear accounts, content to win merit ratings by opening new land and increasing levies for a time while still tolerating arrears without inquiry; he asked that the ministry be ordered to verify;
translations.idiomatic: "Other provinces play at compliance, refuse honest accounting, chase merit by opening wasteland and raising levies for a season, and still leave arrears untouched. I ask the ministry to audit them;"

sentences.zh: 又紳衿抗糧，定有新條，蠹役尤應加嚴，並請敕部定例行。

translations.literal: new rules on gentry resistance to grain tax should also be fixed, and parasites in particular should be tightened; he asked the ministry to set rules and implement.
translations.idiomatic: "new rules on gentry grain resistance should be fixed, and yamen parasites especially should face stricter penalties. I ask the ministry to decree and enforce."

sentences.zh: 」十七年，遷太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: " In the seventeenth year he was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遭父喪。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he mourned his father.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，起補原官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi he returned to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 3 he resumed his former post.

sentences.zh: 六年，疏言：「朝廷欲薄賦，有司反加賦；

translations.literal: In the sixth year he memorialized: "The court wishes to lighten levies, yet local officials increase them;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he wrote: "The court wishes to lighten taxes, yet local officials raise them;"

sentences.zh: 朝廷欲省刑，有司反濫刑：皆由督撫不得其人。

translations.literal: the court wishes to reduce punishments, yet local officials abuse them—all because governors-general and governors are not the right men.
translations.idiomatic: "the court wishes to reduce punishment, yet local officials multiply it—all because the wrong men sit as governors-general and governors."

sentences.zh: 今方有詔令部院糾察，部院肯糾極貪大惡之督撫一人，天下為督撫者警；

translations.literal: Now an edict orders the ministries to investigate; if the ministries will impeach one governor-general or governor who is utterly corrupt and vicious, every governor-general and governor in the realm will take warning;
translations.idiomatic: "An edict now orders the ministries to investigate. If they will impeach one utterly corrupt governor-general or governor, every governor in the realm will tremble;"

sentences.zh: 督撫肯糾極貪大惡之司道一人，天下為司道者警。

translations.literal: if governors-general and governors will impeach one utterly corrupt circuit intendant or prefect, every circuit intendant and prefect will take warning.
translations.idiomatic: "if governors will impeach one utterly corrupt intendant or prefect, every intendant and prefect will tremble."

sentences.zh: 督撫、司道廉潔，則有司不苦誅求，輕徭薄賦，政簡刑清，自寬然有餘地矣。

translations.literal: When governors-general, governors, and circuit officials are clean, subordinates need not squeeze the people; with light corvée and thin levies, simplified government and cleared punishments, there will naturally be room to spare.
translations.idiomatic: "When governors and intendants are clean, subordinates need not extort; light levies and simple punishments leave margin for mercy."

sentences.zh: 」八年，應詔陳民生疾苦，言：「小民莫疾於加派，莫苦於火耗，已敕嚴禁矣。

translations.literal: " In the eighth year, responding to an edict to state the people's hardships, he said: "Among the common people nothing is worse than extra levies, nothing more bitter than surcharge for melting fees—already strictly forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, answering an edict on popular hardship, he said: "Commoners suffer most from surcharges and from melting-fee surcharges—both already forbidden."

sentences.zh: 此外疾苦尚有數端：有司派殷戶催糧，糧單中多列逃亡絕戶，無可徵糧；

translations.literal: Beyond these there are still several other hardships: officials assign wealthy households to press for grain, and on the tax rolls many listed as absconded or extinct households have no grain to collect;
translations.idiomatic: "Beyond those, other griefs remain: magistrates assign rich households to press collection, and tax rolls list many absconded or extinct households from whom no grain can be taken;"

sentences.zh: 且有糧冊無名，按時追比，致傾家以償者。

translations.literal: and when the grain register has no name yet collection is pressed on schedule, families are ruined paying for others.
translations.idiomatic: "yet names absent from the register are still pursued on schedule, ruining families who pay others' debts."

sentences.zh: 郵傳供應，原有錢糧，或侵入私囊，僉民養馬應夫或充里長。

translations.literal: Postal relay supplies originally had allotted funds, yet some officials pocket them privately and press the people to raise horses, supply laborers, or serve as village heads.
translations.idiomatic: "Postal funds exist by statute, yet some officials pocket them and press the people to raise horses, supply labor, or serve as village head."

sentences.zh: 使客往來，舟車飲食，責令設備。

translations.literal: When envoys come and go, boats, carts, food, and drink are all demanded to be provided.
translations.idiomatic: "When travelers pass through, boats, carts, food, and drink must all be furnished at local expense."

sentences.zh: 河漕附近，籍民應役，衣敝履決，力盡筋疲，而工食或至中飽。

translations.literal: Near the Grand Canal commoners are registered for corvée; in ragged clothes and worn shoes, strength spent and sinews exhausted, yet workers' rations are sometimes embezzled midway.
translations.idiomatic: "Along the canal the people are registered for labor in tatters, exhausted, while rations for workers are embezzled on the way."

sentences.zh: 淺夫閘夫，賣富差貧，一名更至數十名，衙役捕系恫哧，民被累無窮。

translations.literal: Shallow-water and lock laborers sell assignments to the rich and assign them to the poor; one name may change to dozens; yamen runners arrest and intimidate, and the people suffer without end.
translations.idiomatic: "Canal coolies sell easy posts to the rich and load the poor; one name becomes dozens; runners arrest and threaten until the harm never ends."

sentences.zh: 請敕督撫清釐懲禁。

translations.literal: He asked that governors-general and governors be ordered to clear accounts and forbid such practices.
translations.idiomatic: He asked governors-general and governors to audit and forbid these abuses.

sentences.zh: 」上納其言，並特諭河工毋得累民。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted his words and also specially instructed that river works must not burden the people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his advice and also expressly ordered that hydraulic works must not burden the people.

sentences.zh: 尋遷右、左通政。

translations.literal: Soon after he was promoted to right and then left vice commissioner of the Court of Imperial Supplications.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to right, then left, vice commissioner of the Court of Imperial Supplications.

sentences.zh: 十一年，疏言：「嘉魚知縣李世錫告湖廣巡撫林天擎索賄，以此知餽遺不絕，苞苴尚行，較世祖朝有司不敢餽遺督撫、不敢輕至省會風氣迥殊。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he memorialized: "Jiayu magistrate Li Shixi reported that Huguang governor Lin Tianqing demanded bribes, showing that gift-giving never ceases and that graft still runs—quite unlike the Shizu era when officials dared not bribe governors-general and governors or lightly visit provincial capitals."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he wrote: "Jiayu magistrate Li Shixi charged Huguang governor Lin Tianqing with demanding bribes—proof that gifts never stop and graft still flows, unlike the Shizu reign when officials dared not bribe governors or casually visit provincial seats."

sentences.zh: 督撫初受命，群餽裘馬、弓矢，而為督撫者亦飾觀瞻、趨奢侈，一時費累萬。

translations.literal: When governors-general and governors first take office, crowds present fur robes, horses, and bows; those who become governors-general and governors also dress for display and rush into extravagance, spending tens of thousands at once.
translations.idiomatic: "When a governor first receives appointment, crowds bring furs, horses, and bows; the new governor himself dresses for show and races into luxury, spending ten thousand at a stroke."

sentences.zh: 上官後，為酬報取償地，遂苛索屬吏，貽累於民。

translations.literal: After taking office, to repay gifts they extort subordinate officials and burden the people.
translations.idiomatic: Once in post, they recover the cost of gifts by squeezing subordinates, and the people bear the harm.

sentences.zh: 請敕督撫赴官之先，屏絕餽送，勿鋪張行色，以儉養廉。

translations.literal: He asked that governors-general and governors, before taking office, refuse all gifts, avoid display in travel, and cultivate integrity through frugality.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that governors, before reporting to their posts, reject gifts, travel without pomp, and keep themselves honest through frugality.

sentences.zh: 督撫參罰科條甚密，部院亦當知督撫艱難繁重，依例處分，毋過為吹索，俾得專心吏治民生，無旁顧之憂。

translations.literal: Rules for governors' impeachment and punishment are very strict; the ministries should also know how arduous governors' duties are, dispose cases by precedent, and not over-investigate, so they may focus on administration and the people's livelihood without distraction.
translations.idiomatic: Impeachment rules for governors are tight, yet the ministries should remember how heavy their burdens are: punish by precedent, do not hunt for faults, and let them concentrate on government and the people.

sentences.zh: 」先後諸疏並下部議行。

translations.literal: " All his successive memorials were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All these memorials in succession were sent to the ministries for deliberation and enactment.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he became vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 十八年，京察，以才力不及擬降調，命再議，改註不謹，遂奪官。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, at the capital review, he was rated as lacking in capacity and slated for demotion; the order was to reconsider; the note was changed to "not diligent" and his office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the capital review found his capacity insufficient and proposed demotion; after reconsideration the verdict was "not diligent" and he lost his post.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，迎蹕臨清，復原銜。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, meeting the imperial procession at Linqing, his former rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year he met the imperial procession at Linqing and had his former rank restored.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，南巡還蹕東昌，幸其所居園，賜松桂堂榜。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, on the southern tour the emperor returned to Dongchang, visited the garden where he lived, and bestowed the plaque Songgui Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year, returning from the southern tour at Dongchang, the emperor visited his home garden and gave the hall the name Songgui.

sentences.zh: 以克溥年將九十，賜刑部尚書銜。

translations.literal: Because Kepu was nearing ninety, the emperor granted him the nominal rank of minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Kepu nearly ninety, the emperor granted him the honorary title of minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 是歲卒，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: That year he died and was granted funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died that year and received state funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十七年，高宗覽克溥條奏諸疏，善之，諭：「克溥逮事兩朝，抒誠建白，無愧直言謇諤之臣。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year of Qianlong, the Gaozong emperor read Kepu's itemized memorials, praised them, and said: "Kepu served two reigns, spoke with sincerity and offered counsel, a forthright remonstrating minister without reproach."
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 47 the emperor read Kepu's policy memorials, approved them, and said: "Kepu served two reigns, spoke plainly and offered sound counsel—a remonstrating minister who need fear no shame."

sentences.zh: 」並命錄諸疏宣示。

translations.literal: " He also ordered the memorials copied and promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the memorials recorded and published for instruction.

sentences.zh: 劉鴻儒，字魯一，直隸遷安人。

translations.literal: Liu Hongru, style name Luyi, was a native of Qian'an in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hongru, courtesy name Luyi, came from Qian'an in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 順治三年進士，授兵科給事中。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the third year of Shunzhi, he was appointed supervising secretary in the military section.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Shunzhi 3 and became a military supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「開國之始，首重安民，宜輕賦徭，革積弊。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "At the founding of the state, settling the people comes first; levies and corvée should be lightened and accumulated abuses reformed."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "At the dynasty's founding the first concern is the people's peace; taxes and labor should be lightened and old abuses swept away."

sentences.zh: 伏讀恩詔，賦制悉依萬曆初年，及觀順治二年徵數，並不減少，且復增重，請敕有司核實。

translations.literal: Having read the grace edict, tax rules were to follow the Wanli early reign; yet viewing the Shunzhi second-year collection figures, they were not reduced and were even increased; he asked that officials be ordered to verify.
translations.idiomatic: "The grace edict says taxes should follow Wanli-era rates, yet Shunzhi 2 collections are no lower and have even risen. I ask that officials verify the truth."

sentences.zh: 州縣六房書吏，初房各二人，今則增至七、八十人，並請敕有司核簡。

translations.literal: In prefectures and counties the six bureaus originally had two clerks each per bureau; now they have increased to seventy or eighty; he also asked officials to verify and reduce.
translations.idiomatic: "County six-bureau clerks once numbered two per bureau; now some offices hold seventy or eighty. I ask that they be audited and cut."

sentences.zh: 」上命指實，鴻儒復言：「臣籍遷安，明季丁銀，下下二錢，下中四錢，上地一畝七分有奇。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered specifics; Hongru replied: "Your subject's home is Qian'an; in late Ming corvée silver for the lowest grade was two qian, lower-middle four qian, and upper land seven fen odd per mu."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor demanded particulars; Hongru answered: "In my home Qian'an, late-Ming corvée for the lowest households was two qian, lower-middle four, upper land about seven fen per mu."

sentences.zh: 民苦輸將，猶多逋賦。

translations.literal: The people suffered in paying and still had much arrears.
translations.idiomatic: People strained to pay and still fell into arrears.

sentences.zh: 今蒙恩詔蠲免，而二年徵數，二錢者增至三錢六分，四錢者增至七錢二分，上地每畝增至八分有奇。

translations.literal: Now under the grace edict remissions are granted, yet second-year collections raise two qian to three qian six fen, four qian to seven qian two fen, and upper land per mu to eight fen odd.
translations.idiomatic: "Now the grace edict promises relief, yet Shunzhi 2 raises two qian to three qian six fen, four to seven qian two fen, and upper land to more than eight fen per mu."

sentences.zh: 一邑如此，他邑可知。

translations.literal: If one county is thus, other counties may be known.
translations.idiomatic: "If one county is so, others surely are as well."

sentences.zh: 乞敕清查蠲免。

translations.literal: He begged that investigation and remission be ordered.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a thorough audit and remission.

sentences.zh: 」下部確察。

translations.literal: " The matter was sent to the ministry for verification.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the ministry for verification.

sentences.zh: 四年，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he moved to revenue.

sentences.zh: 五年，坐糾鉅鹿知縣勞有學失實，左遷上林苑蕃育署署丞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, for impeaching Julu magistrate Lao Youxue on false grounds, he was demoted to assistant director of the Imperial Park Breeding Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was demoted for falsely impeaching Julu magistrate Lao Youxue, becoming assistant director of the imperial park breeding office.

sentences.zh: 十年，命復故官。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was ordered to resume his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 十三年，補兵科，疏言：「畿輔近地，劫掠時聞。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was restored to the military section and memorialized: "In the metropolitan region nearby, robbery is often heard of."
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he returned to the military section and wrote: "Near the capital, highway robbery is still reported."

sentences.zh: 請嚴責成，謹防捕。

translations.literal: He asked that responsibility be strictly enforced and capture carefully guarded.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for strict accountability and tighter policing.

sentences.zh: 」下部如所請。

translations.literal: " The ministry acted as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry did as he asked.

sentences.zh: 轉戶科，十五年，疏言：「開國以來，度支屢見不敷。

translations.literal: He transferred to the revenue section; in the fifteenth year he memorialized: "Since the founding, revenue has repeatedly fallen short."
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the revenue section; in the fifteenth year he wrote: "Since the founding, the treasury has repeatedly run short."

sentences.zh: 汱冗員，增榷務，廣輸納，督積逋，講求開節，已無不盡。

translations.literal: Cutting redundant posts, increasing transit duties, broadening purchase contributions, pressing arrears, and seeking every economy—nothing has been left undone.
translations.idiomatic: "Redundant posts were cut, transit levies raised, purchase offices widened, arrears pressed, every saving tried—nothing remains unused."

sentences.zh: 今南服削平，萬方底定，宜總計財賦之數，准其出入，定為經久不易之規。

translations.literal: Now the south is pacified and the realm settled; revenue and expenditure should be totaled, income and outgo fixed, and a lasting rule established.
translations.idiomatic: "The south is pacified and the realm at rest. Total revenue and spending, fix income against outgo, and set a lasting rule."

sentences.zh: 請通計一歲內畝賦、丁徭、鹽徵、津稅，各省輕齎、重運及贖鍰事例等項，汰其猥瑣無藝者，所存金粟若干數；

translations.literal: He asked that within one year land tax, corvée, salt levies, transit taxes, each province's light and heavy transport, fine-redemption precedents, and the like be totaled, petty and useless items cut, and the remaining gold and grain counted;
translations.idiomatic: "Total within one year land tax, corvée, salt, transit duties, provincial transport, fines, and the like; cut petty waste; count what gold and grain remain;"

sentences.zh: 然後計一歲內上方供應、官吏俸祿、兵馬糧料、朝祭禮儀、修築工役，以至師生廩餼、胥役代食，罷其不經無益者，所需金粟若干數：務使出入相合，定為會計之準。

translations.literal: then within one year court supply, official salaries, troop grain, ritual and sacrifice, construction labor, down to students' stipends and clerks' substitute rations—abolish what is irregular and useless, count what gold and grain are needed: income and outgo must match and become the standard of accounts.
translations.idiomatic: "then total court supply, salaries, army grain, ritual, construction, students' stipends, clerks' rations—cut what is irregular; count what is needed: income and outgo must balance and become the fiscal standard."

sentences.zh: 用財大端惟兵，生財本計惟土。

translations.literal: The great outlet for spending is troops; the root of producing wealth is land.
translations.idiomatic: "Spending centers on the army; wealth centers on the soil."

sentences.zh: 欲紓國計，莫善於屯田，朝廷下民屯之令。

translations.literal: To ease state finances, nothing is better than garrison farming; the court issued orders for civilian farming colonies.
translations.idiomatic: "To ease the treasury, garrison farming is best; the court has ordered civilian colonies."

sentences.zh: 設官置役，多糜廩祿，得不償失，不旋踵而請罷。

translations.literal: Officials and labor were appointed, consuming much grain salary; gains did not repay costs; before long they asked to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet officials and staff were appointed, salaries eaten up, costs exceeded gains, and soon the scheme was abandoned."

sentences.zh: 稽古屯制，不在民而在兵，請敕各省駐兵處所，無論邊腹地方，察有荒土，令兵充種。

translations.literal: Examining ancient colony rules, colonies lay not with civilians but with troops; he asked that wherever troops were stationed in each province, whether frontier or interior, idle land be found and troops made to farm.
translations.idiomatic: "Ancient colonies used soldiers, not civilians. Order every garrison, frontier or interior, to farm idle land with its troops."

sentences.zh: 正疆界，信賞罰，則趨事自力；

translations.literal: Fix boundaries, trust rewards and punishments, and men will exert themselves;
translations.idiomatic: "Fix boundaries, keep rewards and punishments honest, and men will labor willingly;"

sentences.zh: 豐種具，寬程效，則收穫自充。

translations.literal: with ample seed and relaxed quotas, harvests will fill needs themselves.
translations.idiomatic: "give seed and ease quotas, and harvests will feed the camps themselves."

sentences.zh: 此唐初府兵之制也。

translations.literal: This is the Tang early fubing system.
translations.idiomatic: "That is the early Tang fubing system."

sentences.zh: 自頃四川、貴州已入版圖，所得之地，必需駐守；

translations.literal: Recently Sichuan and Guizhou have entered the map; land gained requires garrison;
translations.idiomatic: "Sichuan and Guizhou are now in the map and must be garrisoned;"

sentences.zh: 若令處處興屯，則根本自固，戰守咸資。

translations.literal: if colonies are raised everywhere, the root will be firm and both defense and offense supplied.
translations.idiomatic: "raise colonies everywhere and the base is firm, defense and offense both supplied."

sentences.zh: 此又趙充國之於先零，杜預之於宛、葉，確然可循之遺策也。

translations.literal: This is also the sure legacy of Zhao Chongguo against the Qiang and Du Yu at Wan and Ye.
translations.idiomatic: "This follows Zhao Chongguo against the Qiang and Du Yu at Wan and Ye—proven policy."

sentences.zh: 順天左右郡縣，拱翊王畿，根本要地，自令舊人圈住，深得居重馭輕之意。

translations.literal: The counties around Shuntian, guarding the capital, are a root place; letting old inhabitants enclose land embodied the idea of weight at the center and lightness at the rim.
translations.idiomatic: "Shuntian counties guard the capital; banner enclosures there embodied holding the center and lightening the rim."

sentences.zh: 但畿輔之民，多失恆業，撥補他地，皆有係屬，豈能據為己有？

translations.literal: Yet metropolitan people have lost their livelihoods; reallocating them elsewhere all have ties—how can they be held as private property?
translations.idiomatic: "Yet capital people have lost livelihoods; moving them elsewhere fails because every plot has owners—how can newcomers claim it?"

sentences.zh: 今喜峰、冷口諸關外，大寧以南，彌望千里，咸稱膏壤，請令民原出關開墾者，許承為己業。

translations.literal: Beyond Xifeng and Lengkou passes, south of Daining, for a thousand li all is called fertile soil; he asked that civilians willing to leave the pass and open land be allowed to hold it as their own.
translations.idiomatic: "Beyond Xifeng and Lengkou, south of Daining, a thousand li of fertile soil lies idle. Let willing civilians who leave the pass farm it and hold it as their own."

sentences.zh: 沃土新闢，獲利必饒，先事有獲，趨者自眾。

translations.literal: Newly opened rich soil must yield abundant profit; gain comes before effort and crowds will follow.
translations.idiomatic: "New rich soil yields profit; success draws settlers of itself."

sentences.zh: 數年以後，漸次起科，成聚成邑，堪資保障。

translations.literal: After several years tax may gradually be levied, settlements and towns formed, and security gained.
translations.idiomatic: "In a few years levy tax by stages, build towns, and secure the frontier."

sentences.zh: 二者皆軍國大計，若設誠致行，久之兵食充足，國基賴以不拔矣。

translations.literal: Both are great plans for state and army; if carried out in earnest, in time army grain will be ample and the foundation unshaken.
translations.idiomatic: "Both are state plans; earnestly carried out, army grain will fill and the foundation stand firm."

sentences.zh: 」下部議，以滇、黔未靖，兵餉無數，難以預定會計；

translations.literal: " The ministry deliberated: with Yunnan and Guizhou not yet pacified, troop pay cannot be numbered, and accounts cannot be fixed in advance;
translations.idiomatic: The ministry replied that with Yunnan and Guizhou unsettled, army pay could not be fixed in advance;

sentences.zh: 設置兵屯，及畿輔民出邊墾種，敕所司詳勘。

translations.literal: establishing troop colonies and metropolitan civilians farming beyond the border were ordered to the relevant offices for detailed survey.
translations.idiomatic: troop colonies and capital civilians farming beyond the passes were sent to the offices for detailed survey.

sentences.zh: 十七年，遷順天府府丞，再遷左通政。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to vice director of the Shuntian prefectural government, then to left vice commissioner of the Court of Imperial Supplications.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he became Shuntian vice prefect, then left vice commissioner of the Court of Imperial Supplications.

sentences.zh: 十八年，遷太常寺卿。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he became president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，遷通政使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi he was promoted to commissioner of the Court of Imperial Supplications.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 3 he became commissioner of the Court of Imperial Supplications.

sentences.zh: 六年，擢兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was elevated to vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 十年，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he moved to revenue.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷左都御史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to left censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he became left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 官戶部時，甘肅巡撫華善因擅發倉粟賑災，戶部循例題參，並議罰償，鴻儒無異議；

translations.literal: When he was at revenue, Gansu governor Hua Shan, for issuing granary grain without authorization to relieve disaster, was impeached by revenue by precedent and also fined for compensation; Hongru raised no objection;
translations.idiomatic: At revenue, Gansu governor Hua Shan was impeached by precedent for issuing granary grain without leave to relieve disaster, with a fine proposed; Hongru did not dissent;

sentences.zh: 及官都御史，又疏論華善不應參處，嗣後封疆大臣有利民之政，不宜拘以文法。

translations.literal: when he was censor-in-chief he again memorialized that Hua Shan should not be punished, and that hereafter frontier grandees with policies benefiting the people should not be bound by formal rules.
translations.idiomatic: as censor-in-chief he wrote that Hua Shan should not be punished and that frontier officials with policies that help the people should not be trapped by paperwork.

sentences.zh: 給事成性疏劾，下部議，坐鴻儒先未異議，後又指摘沽名，降二級調用。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Cheng Xing memorialized; the ministry deliberated; Hongru was sentenced for first raising no objection and later impeaching for reputation, demoted two ranks and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Cheng Xing impeached him; the ministry found Hongru first silent, then critical for reputation, and demoted him two ranks.

sentences.zh: 尋卒於家。

translations.literal: Soon after he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at home.

sentences.zh: 劉楗，字玉罍，直隸大城人。

translations.literal: Liu Jian, style name Yuzan, was a native of Dacheng in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian, courtesy name Yuzan, came from Dacheng in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 順治二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the second year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Shunzhi 2.

sentences.zh: 是歲選新進士十人授給事中，楗除戶科。

translations.literal: That year ten new jinshi were chosen as supervising secretaries; Jian was assigned to the revenue section.
translations.idiomatic: That year ten new jinshi were made supervising secretaries; Jian took the revenue section.

sentences.zh: 疏論山東巡撫楊聲遠劾青州道韓昭宣受賄釋叛賊十四人，僅令住俸勦賊，罰不蔽辜，昭宣坐奪官。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Shandong governor Yang Shengyuan impeached Qingzhou circuit intendant Han Zhaoxuan for taking bribes to release fourteen rebel bandits, only ordering salary withheld and bandits suppressed—the penalty did not cover the crime; Zhaoxuan was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He charged Shandong governor Yang Shengyuan for impeaching Han Zhaoxuan of taking bribes to free fourteen rebels while only withholding salary and ordering suppression—the penalty was too light, and Zhaoxuan lost his post.

sentences.zh: 四年，轉兵科右給事中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he transferred to right supervising secretary of the military section.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became right supervising secretary of the military section.

sentences.zh: 疏論江南巡按宋調元薦舉泰州游擊潘延吉，寇至棄城走，調元濫舉失當，亦坐奪官。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Jiangnan touring censor Song Diaoyuan recommended Taizhou battalion commander Pan Yanji, who when bandits came abandoned the city and fled; Diaoyuan's recommendation was improper and he too was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He charged Jiangnan censor Song Diaoyuan for recommending Pan Yanji, who fled when bandits came; Song's recommendation was reckless and he too lost his post.

sentences.zh: 是歲大計，楗用拾遺例，揭山東聊城知縣張守廉贓款，下所司勘議，守廉以失察吏役得贓，罰俸；

translations.literal: That year at the great review Jian used the remnant-exposure precedent to expose Liaocheng magistrate Zhang Shoulian for embezzlement; the case was sent for investigation; Shoulian was fined for failing to supervise clerks who took bribes;
translations.idiomatic: At the great review Jian used the remnant-exposure rule to expose Zhang Shoulian of Liaocheng for embezzlement; Zhang was fined for failing to supervise clerks who took bribes;

sentences.zh: 楗誣糾，坐奪官。

translations.literal: Jian was impeached for false accusation and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was impeached for a false charge and lost his post.

sentences.zh: 十年，吏科都給事中魏象樞請行大計拾遺，因論楗枉，得旨，吏役詐贓，知縣僅罰俸，言官反坐奪官，明有冤抑，令吏部察奏，命以原官起用。

translations.literal: In the tenth year chief supervising secretary of the personnel section Wei Xiangqi asked to apply great-review remnant exposure; citing Jian's injustice, he received an edict: when clerks fraudulently embezzle and the magistrate is only fined, yet the censor loses office, injustice is clear; the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to investigate and report; he was ordered reappointed to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Wei Xiangqi urged remnant exposure at the great review and cited Jian's injustice; the emperor said that when clerks embezzle by fraud and the magistrate is only fined while the censor loses office, injustice is plain; personnel was ordered to investigate and Jian was restored.

sentences.zh: 授兵科左給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed left supervising secretary of the military section.
translations.idiomatic: He was made left supervising secretary of the military section.

sentences.zh: 十一年，疏言：「近畿被水地，水落地可耕。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he memorialized: "In the metropolitan region where water has receded, the land can be farmed."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he wrote: "Near the capital, flooded land has dried and can be planted."

sentences.zh: 方春農事急，請敕巡撫檄州縣發存留銀，借災民籽種，俟秋成責償。

translations.literal: Spring farming is urgent; he asked that the governor order prefectures and counties to issue retained silver and lend seed to disaster victims, to be repaid after autumn harvest.
translations.idiomatic: "Spring planting is urgent. Let the governor order counties to lend retained funds for seed and collect after harvest."

sentences.zh: 仍飭巡行鄉村勘覈，不使吏胥得緣以為利。

translations.literal: Patrols in villages should also be ordered so clerks cannot profit from the scheme.
translations.idiomatic: "Order village inspections so clerks cannot profit from the loans."

sentences.zh: 十二年，疏言：「鄭成功蹂躪漳、泉，窺伺省會。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he memorialized: "Zheng Chenggong ravaged Zhang and Quan and watched the provincial capital."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he wrote: "Zheng Chenggong ravages Zhangzhou and Quanzhou and eyes the provincial seat."

sentences.zh: 臣昔充福建考官，詢悉地勢。

translations.literal: Your subject once served as Fujian examiner and inquired into the terrain.
translations.idiomatic: "I once examined in Fujian and know the terrain."

sentences.zh: 福清鎮東衛，明時駐兵防倭。

translations.literal: At Fuqing, Zhendong Guard, Ming troops were stationed against Japanese pirates.
translations.idiomatic: "At Fuqing's Zhendong Guard the Ming posted troops against pirates."

sentences.zh: 倘復舊制，可以保障長樂，籓衛會城。

translations.literal: If the old system is restored, Changle can be secured and the provincial seat shielded.
translations.idiomatic: "Restore that garrison and Changle is secured and the capital shielded."

sentences.zh: 宋、元設州海壇，明以倭患棄之。

translations.literal: Song and Yuan had a Haitan prefecture; Ming abandoned it because of Japanese trouble.
translations.idiomatic: "Song and Yuan held Haitan; the Ming abandoned it to Japanese raids."

sentences.zh: 若設將鎮守，可與鎮東互為犄角。

translations.literal: If a general is stationed there, it can form a pincer with Zhendong.
translations.idiomatic: "Station a general there and it pincers with Zhendong."

sentences.zh: 仙霞嶺為入福建門戶，與江西、浙江接壤，宜設官控制，招民以實其地，俾無隙可乘。

translations.literal: Xianxia Ridge is the gateway into Fujian, bordering Jiangxi and Zhejiang; officials should be posted to control it, people recruited to fill the land, leaving no gap.
translations.idiomatic: "Xianxia Ridge is Fujian's gate, touching Jiangxi and Zhejiang; post officials, settle people, and leave no gap."

sentences.zh: 成功數犯京口，泊舟平洋沙為巢穴。

translations.literal: Chenggong repeatedly struck Jingkou and moored at Pingyang Shoal as a nest.
translations.idiomatic: "Chenggong has struck Jingkou repeatedly and nests at Pingyang Shoal."

sentences.zh: 宜乘其未至，移兵駐鎮，使退無可據，必不敢深入內地。

translations.literal: Troops should be moved to garrison before he arrives so he has no foothold on retreat and dare not penetrate inland.
translations.idiomatic: "Move troops there before he comes so he has no refuge and dare not push inland."

sentences.zh: 」疏入，敕鎮海將軍石廷柱等分別駐守。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, Coastal Defense General Shi Tingzhu and others were ordered to garrison separately.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went in and Coastal Defense General Shi Tingzhu and others were ordered to garrison as proposed.

sentences.zh: 十三年，授山西河東道副使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed vice commissioner of the Shanxi Hedong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he became vice commissioner of the Shanxi Hedong circuit.

sentences.zh: 十五年，轉河南鹽驛道參議。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he transferred to Henan salt and courier intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he became Henan salt and courier intendant.

sentences.zh: 十六年，授湖廣按察使，就遷右布政。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Huguang provincial judicial commissioner and soon promoted to right provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he became Huguang judicial commissioner and soon right administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十八年，總督張長庚、巡撫楊茂勳疏薦楗廉幹，協濟滇、黔兵餉至八百餘萬，清逋賦墾地，除鼓鑄積弊。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Governor-General Zhang Changgeng and Governor Yang Maoxun memorialized recommending Jian as incorrupt and capable, assisting Yunnan-Guizhou troop pay to more than eight million, clearing arrears and opening land, and removing accumulated abuses in coinage.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Zhang Changgeng and Yang Maoxun recommended Jian as clean and capable, having helped pay more than eight million for Yunnan-Guizhou troops, cleared arrears, opened land, and ended coinage abuses.

sentences.zh: 楗以母憂歸。

translations.literal: Jian returned home for mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Jian went home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，起江西布政使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi he was recalled as Jiangxi administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 2 he returned as Jiangxi administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂亂作，措餉供兵，事辦而民不擾。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui rebelled, he arranged funds and supplied the army; affairs were handled and the people were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled he raised funds and supplied the army without disturbing the people.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授太常寺卿。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he became president of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遷大理寺卿。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he became president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 十七年，擢副都御史，疏言：「自吳三桂為亂，軍需旁午，大計暫停。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief and memorialized: "Since Wu Sangui's rebellion, military needs have come in waves and the great review was suspended."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he became vice censor-in-chief and wrote: "Since Wu Sangui rebelled, military needs have flooded in and the great review stopped."

sentences.zh: 今師所至，漸次蕩平。

translations.literal: " Now wherever the army reaches, order is gradually restored.
translations.idiomatic: "Now wherever the army advances, order returns."

sentences.zh: 伏思兵後殘壞已極，正賴賢有司招徠安輯。

translations.literal: Your subject reflects that after war ruin is extreme and worthy magistrates are needed to summon and settle the people.
translations.idiomatic: "After war ruin is extreme; worthy magistrates are needed to summon and settle the people."

sentences.zh: 若使不肖用事，何以澄吏治、奠民生、息盜賊？

translations.literal: If unworthy men hold office, how can official discipline be cleared, the people settled, and bandits quieted?
translations.idiomatic: "If unworthy men rule, how can government be purified, the people secured, and bandits stilled?"

sentences.zh: 請令督撫速行舉劾，凡經薦舉者，改行易操，一體嚴察，不得偏徇。

translations.literal: He asked that governors-general and governors quickly conduct recommendations and impeachments; all who have been recommended must change conduct under strict scrutiny without partiality.
translations.idiomatic: He asked governors to speed recommendations and impeachments, and to scrutinize even former favorites without favoritism.

sentences.zh: 」下部如所請行。

translations.literal: " The ministry acted as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry did as he asked.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「江西當亂後，民逃田墟，錢糧缺額不急予蠲免，逃者不歸，歸者復逃；

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "After rebellion in Jiangxi the people fled and fields lay waste; if tax shortfalls are not promptly remitted, those who fled will not return and those who return will flee again;
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "After Jiangxi's rebellion people fled and fields lay waste. Unless tax shortfalls are remitted at once, fugitives will not return and returnees will flee again;"

sentences.zh: 荒者未墾，墾者仍荒​​。

translations.literal: what is waste is not reclaimed, and what is reclaimed becomes waste again.
translations.idiomatic: "wasteland stays untilled, and tilled land turns waste again."

sentences.zh: 」上為特旨悉行蠲免。

translations.literal: " The emperor issued a special edict granting full remission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a special edict granting full remission.

sentences.zh: 旋以病乞休，諭慰留，遣太醫視疾。

translations.literal: Soon after, ill, he begged to retire; the emperor comforted him and kept him, sending an imperial physician to treat his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fell ill and asked to retire; the emperor urged him to stay and sent an imperial physician.

sentences.zh: 擢吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 未幾，复擢刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was again promoted to minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 十八年，病劇，始得請還裡。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year his illness grew severe and he was at last permitted to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year his illness worsened and he was finally allowed to go home.

sentences.zh: 至家，卒，賜祭葬，諡端敏。

translations.literal: Upon reaching home he died; funeral rites were granted and his posthumous title was Duanmin.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home; the court granted funeral honors and the posthumous name Duanmin.

sentences.zh: 硃裴，字小晉，山西聞喜人。

translations.literal: Zhu Pei, style name Xiaojin, was a native of Wenxi in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Pei, courtesy name Xiaojin, came from Wenxi in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 亦順治三年進士。

translations.literal: Also a jinshi in the third year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He too passed the jinshi in Shunzhi 3.

sentences.zh: 知直隸易州，移河南禹州。

translations.literal: He was magistrate of Yizhou in Zhili, then transferred to Yuzhou in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Yizhou in Zhili, then Yuzhou in Henan.

sentences.zh: 裴治尚嚴，到官即捕殺盜渠。

translations.literal: Pei's governance favored severity; upon taking office he captured and executed bandit chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Pei ran a strict administration; on taking office he captured and executed bandit leaders.

sentences.zh: 縣有諸生聘婦為盜掠，既復自歸。

translations.literal: In the county a licentiate's betrothed was seized by bandits and later returned of her own accord.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate's fiancée was seized by bandits and later returned on her own.

sentences.zh: 盜以奪婦訟生，婦以生貧且別娶，反為盜證。

translations.literal: The bandit sued the licentiate for seizing his woman; the woman, finding the licentiate poor and already married elsewhere, testified for the bandit.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit sued the licentiate for stealing his woman; she, finding the licentiate poor and wed elsewhere, testified against him.

sentences.zh: 前政論生死，裴廉得實，為榜殺婦而出生於獄。

translations.literal: The previous magistrate debated life and death; Pei, investigating cleanly, got the facts, posted a notice executing the woman and released the licentiate from prison.
translations.idiomatic: The prior magistrate had debated capital guilt; Pei investigated fairly, had the woman executed on the placard, and freed the licentiate.

sentences.zh: 擢刑部員外郎，遷廣東道御史，再遷禮科給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Justice, transferred to Guangdong circuit censor, and again to rites-section supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to justice vice director, became Guangdong circuit censor, then rites supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 滿洲俗尚殉葬，裴疏請申禁，略言：「泥信幽明，未有如此之甚者。

translations.literal: Manchu custom favored funeral sacrifice; Pei memorialized to forbid it, saying in brief: "Clinging to belief in the nether world—never has it been carried so far."
translations.idiomatic: Manchu custom favored burial sacrifice; Pei memorialized to forbid it: "Faith in the shades has never been pushed so far."

sentences.zh: 夫以主命責問奴僕，或畏威而不敢不從，或懷德而不忍不從，二者俱不可為訓。

translations.literal: When the master's command compels slaves and servants, some obey from fear and dare not refuse, some from gratitude and cannot bear to refuse—neither may serve as teaching.
translations.idiomatic: "When masters command slaves, some obey from fear, some from gratitude—neither should be our model."

sentences.zh: 好生惡死，人之常情。

translations.literal: Loving life and hating death is the constant feeling of men.
translations.idiomatic: "Loving life and fearing death is human nature."

sentences.zh: 捐軀輕生，非盛世所宜有。

translations.literal: Throwing away the body and lightly ending life is not what a flourishing age should have.
translations.idiomatic: "Throwing life away lightly is not fit for a flourishing age."

sentences.zh: 」疏入，報可。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, approval was reported.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 累遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 以疾乞休，歸。

translations.literal: Ill, he begged to retire and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Illness led him to retire and return home.

sentences.zh: 地震，傷於足，臥家九年，卒。

translations.literal: In an earthquake his foot was injured; he lay at home nine years and died.
translations.idiomatic: An earthquake injured his foot; he lay at home nine years and died.

sentences.zh: 張廷樞，字景峰，陝西韓城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Tingshu, style name Jingfeng, was a native of Hancheng in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tingshu, courtesy name Jingfeng, came from Hancheng in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 父顧行，康熙六年進士，官江安督糧道。

translations.literal: His father Guhang, a jinshi in the sixth year of Kangxi, was grain-supervision commissioner of Jiang'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guhang, jinshi of Kangxi 6, was Jiang'an grain commissioner.

sentences.zh: 廷樞，二十一年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Tingshu, a jinshi in the twenty-first year, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Tingshu took his jinshi in Kangxi 21, entered the Hanlin Academy, and became a compiler.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，以侍讀主江南鄉試。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year, as reader-in-waiting, he chaired the Jiangnan provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year he chaired the Jiangnan provincial examination as reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，以內閣學士督江南學政。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, as Grand Secretariat academician, he supervised Jiangnan education.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year he supervised Jiangnan education as a Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，聖祖南巡，賜御書、冠服。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year, on the Sacred Ancestor's southern tour, imperial calligraphy and court dress were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fourth year, during Kangxi's southern tour, he received imperial calligraphy and court dress.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，遷吏部侍郎，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was transferred to vice minister of personnel and appointed lecturer at the imperial lecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he became vice minister of personnel and imperial lecturer.

sentences.zh: 湖廣容美土司田舜年揭其子昺如貪庸暴戾，昺如匿桑植土司向長庚所，不赴鞫。

translations.literal: Rongmei native chieftain Tian Shunnian of Huguang exposed his son Bingru as greedy, mediocre, and cruel; Bingru hid with Sangzhi chieftain Xiang Changgeng and would not appear for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang's Rongmei chieftain Tian Shunnian accused his son Bingru of greed, mediocrity, and cruelty; Bingru hid with Sangzhi chieftain Xiang Changgeng and refused trial.

sentences.zh: 總督石文晟以聞，並劾舜年僭妄。

translations.literal: Governor-General Shi Wencheng reported it and also impeached Shunnian for presumption.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Shi Wencheng reported this and also impeached Shunnian for arrogance.

sentences.zh: 命左都御史梅鋗、內閣學士二格會文晟按治。

translations.literal: Left Censor-in-Chief Mei Mei and Grand Secretariat academician Erge were ordered to join Wencheng in investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Left Censor-in-Chief Mei Mei and academician Erge were ordered to join Wencheng in investigation.

sentences.zh: 舜年詣武昌，文晟執之，病卒。

translations.literal: Shunnian came to Wuchang; Wencheng detained him and he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Shunnian came to Wuchang; Wencheng detained him and he died in custody.

sentences.zh: 鋗與文晟各具議疏陳，二格疏言佐證未集，未可即定議。

translations.literal: Mei and Wencheng each submitted deliberation memorials; Erge memorialized that corroboration was not yet gathered and judgment could not yet be fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Mei and Wencheng each submitted findings; Erge said corroboration was incomplete and judgment premature.

sentences.zh: 詔廷樞偕大學士席哈納、侍郎蕭永藻覆勘，舜年各款俱虛，梅鋗以草率具奏，下部議奪官；

translations.literal: Tingshu was ordered with Grand Secretary Xihana and Vice Minister Xiao Yongzao to re-investigate; every charge against Shunnian was false; Mei Mei was referred to the ministry for careless memorializing and office stripped;
translations.idiomatic: Tingshu was sent with Xihana and Xiao Yongzao to reinvestigate; every charge against Shunnian proved false; Mei Mei lost his post for careless reporting;

sentences.zh: 文晟及湖北巡撫劉殿衡、偏沅巡撫趙申喬、提督俞益謨各降罰有差。

translations.literal: Wencheng and Huguang Governor Liu Dianheng, Pianyuan Governor Zhao Shenqiao, and Provincial Military Commissioner Yu Yimo were each demoted or fined in differing degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng, Liu Dianheng, Zhao Shenqiao, and Yu Yimo were demoted or fined in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，進刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he was promoted to minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year he became minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 民張三等盜倉米，步軍統領託合齊逮送刑部，滿尚書齊世武擬斬監候，廷樞持不可，擬充軍。

translations.literal: Commoner Zhang San and others stole granary grain; Steppe Army Commander Tuheqi arrested and sent them to justice; Manchu Minister Qishiwu proposed deferred decapitation; Tingshu objected and proposed military exile.
translations.idiomatic: Commoner Zhang San and others stole granary grain; Steppe Army Commander Tuheqi sent them to justice; Manchu minister Qishiwu proposed death deferred; Tingshu objected and proposed military exile.

sentences.zh: 下九卿議，廷樞改擬不當，當罰俸。

translations.literal: Referred to the Nine Ministers for deliberation, Tingshu's revised sentence was improper and he should forfeit salary.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Ministers found Tingshu's revised sentence improper and fined his salary.

sentences.zh: 上責廷樞偏執好勝，奪官。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Tingshu as stubborn and contentious and stripped his office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Tingshu as stubborn and contentious and stripped his office.
